idiom_name: Component abstraction + Leaf + Composite holding a child collection
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: declare one Component abstraction carrying the operations clients should invoke uniformly (size/cost, render, validate, serialise, traverse), implement it directly in the leaf nodes, and in a container node that holds a collection of Components and implements the same operations by delegating to each child and combining the results. Write clients against Component only. Decide deliberately where child management lives: on Component it buys transparency and forces leaves into no-op or throwing stubs (the classic mistake); on the container it preserves type safety and costs one cast or subtype test at the few places that edit structure - prefer the safe placement and provide a composite predicate for those places.
pitfalls: Declaring child management on Component so that leaves must implement meaningless add/remove methods - the interface stops meaning anything and LSP breaks.
Letting one node be a child of two parents without an ownership rule: the same subtree is destroyed twice or mutated from one side of the tree.
Allowing a node to be inserted into its own descendant, which turns traversal into infinite recursion.
